answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by charging a forfeitable bond per identity, funded from a distinct lineage, so a thousand puppets cost a thousand separate stakes before any work counts. A fake identity must then earn trust through a voyage of vouched jobs from zero, so cloning names buys nothing. Each action is hashed into a kernel that peers can replay, and prior quartz-grade work history proves a newcomer is real. The attacker's cost scales with identity count while reward stays flat, making swarms unprofitable.
